title.en: Accessible museum route and object inspection

summary: Build a navigable gallery whose route, landmarks and exhibit inspection stay connected, with equivalent controls for essential spatial actions and venue-specific clearance assumptions kept explicit.
objective: Let a visitor choose a landmark, travel or jump to it, inspect the same exhibit from an appropriate view, read its interpretation, and return or reset without losing orientation.

claims.statement: The Smithsonian exhibition guideline calls for an accessible circulation route, gives 915 mm as its minimum one-way clear width and recommends 1525 mm even for one-way routes so a wheelchair user can stop at a case without blocking the route; it also gives an approximately 760 by 1220 mm clear floor space at viewing sides of cases and vitrines.
claims.scope: Smithsonian physical exhibition guidance used only as one declared layout preset. It is not a universal rule for virtual navigation, a substitute for local codes or visitor testing, or evidence that a rendered gallery is accessible.

source_refs.locator: Smithsonian Guidelines for Accessible Design, III Circulation Route, especially Figures 21-23 and the paragraphs on route width and case viewing floor space

claims.statement: For web content, WCAG 2.2 requires functionality to be operable through a keyboard interface except for path-dependent input, requires a visible keyboard-focus indicator, and requires that merely receiving focus not initiate a change of context.
claims.scope: Normative web-interface criteria relevant to labeled controls around a 3D view. The recipe does not claim WCAG conformance, and free camera motion may still use pointer gestures when equivalent task outcomes are available through controls.

source_refs.locator: Success Criteria 2.1.1 Keyboard, 2.4.7 Focus Visible, and 3.2.1 On Focus

entities.name: Gallery route graph
entities.guidance: Use stable landmark nodes and traversable segments in one declared coordinate system; keep stairs, lifts, ramps, shortcuts and blocked segments semantically distinct rather than drawing one decorative floor line.

entities.name: Exhibit station
entities.guidance: Bind the display object, case or mount, label, viewing anchor and optional alternate-description content to one stable exhibit ID.

entities.name: Visitor and camera
entities.guidance: Keep route position, facing, active landmark, selected exhibit and inspection camera separate so inspection cannot silently teleport the authoritative visitor state.

entities.name: Navigation and interpretation controls
entities.guidance: Provide a labeled landmark list and inspection controls with visible focus; selecting a control previews or focuses it, while activation performs navigation or opens the exhibit.

state_contract.model: One reducer owns route position, facing, route plan, selected exhibit ID, navigation mode, inspection mode, camera presentation, content alternative and saved return view. Route travel and named-view jumps are explicit different actions. Entering inspection snapshots the route camera; leaving restores that snapshot without rewinding route state. Reset restores the declared entrance, default route options, no selection and the initial camera.
state_contract.authority: Application state keyed by stable route-node and exhibit IDs is authoritative. Render meshes, focus rings, floor highlights and camera tweens derive from it and never mutate visitor position by themselves.
actions: Choose a landmark from the map or labeled list
Move along a valid route segment or activate a named-view jump
Select and activate an exhibit through pointer or keyboard-operable controls
Enter inspection, choose an authored object view and open the label or alternate description
Return to the saved route view without changing route progress
Reset navigation, selection, inspection and presentation state to the declared entrance snapshot

intent_signals: build a museum I can navigate without precise dragging
let visitors inspect artifacts and return to the gallery
show an accessible exhibition route with keyboard controls
make a virtual gallery with landmarks and object descriptions
example_prompts: Create a small virtual museum with three landmark exhibits, a labeled keyboard route, inspectable objects and a reliable return-to-gallery action.
Model a gallery layout using a declared Smithsonian clearance preset, then show the route envelope and let me switch to a venue-specific preset.
negative_signals: automatic flythrough with no visitor choice
museum facade without an interior route
claim of accessibility based only on visual appearance
not_for: Certifying a real building, local-code compliance or assistive-technology conformance without project-specific evaluation.
Large collection-management systems where the task is catalog search rather than spatial navigation and inspection.
A path-accurate mobility training simulation unless movement, controls and collision behavior are separately validated.
invariants: Every landmark exposed as reachable has a valid route or an explicit unavailable reason; a decorative line is not route evidence.
Selected exhibit identity survives overview, travel, inspection, alternate content and return; mesh replacement cannot select a neighbor by array index.
Keyboard focus is visible and does not itself navigate, open an exhibit or move the camera; activation causes the declared action.
Pointer and labeled-control paths reach the same essential landmarks and exhibit states, though free-form orbit trajectories need not match.
Leaving inspection restores the saved route view and preserves route position; reset restores the complete entrance snapshot.
Any clearance overlay names its source or venue preset, units and scope; changing the preset recomputes the route envelope rather than relabeling unchanged geometry.
motion_guidance: Use short, interruptible transitions between route and inspection views; a new navigation action cancels the old transition from the currently rendered camera.
Offer immediate focus and named viewpoints when reduced motion is requested; do not make automatic camera travel necessary to obtain the exhibit content.
Keep ambient exhibit motion paused or independent during close inspection when it would obscure the object; motion must not carry the only selection or route cue.
creative_affordances: The gallery may be realistic, miniature, abstract or impossible, provided routes, landmarks and inspection relationships remain readable.
Use floor texture, lighting rhythm, room silhouette or recurring motifs as redundant landmarks rather than relying on color alone.
Offer optional curated routes by duration or theme, but preserve free landmark selection and disclose any unreachable station.
known_limits: The cited Smithsonian dimensions are institution-specific physical exhibition guidance and may be superseded by local requirements or a project accessibility brief.
WCAG criteria apply to the web interface; this authored recipe has not been tested with a keyboard, screen reader, switch device, magnifier, wheelchair user or other museum visitor.
A text description, named views and keyboard controls improve available paths but do not establish universal design or conformance.
No route solver, renderer, museum artifact, usability study or runtime interaction was executed for this draft.

object_craft.structure: Separate plinth, support mount, transparent enclosure, frame, opening seam and label rail so the protected object and the case do not merge into one block.
object_craft.material: Use restrained glass transmission and reflections with enough edge/frame contrast to reveal the enclosure; keep the artifact readable through the case.
object_craft.articulation: Inspection may hide or ghost the enclosure as an explicitly labeled presentation mode; it does not imply opening or removing a real conservation case.

object_craft.structure: Build a recognizable whole-room feature with a silhouette visible at route height and a corresponding icon or name in the landmark list.
object_craft.material: Differentiate it through form, texture and value as well as hue so it remains useful under varied lighting and color perception.

physical_contract.scope: Optional continuous route travel uses a controlled visitor proxy against authored walkable surfaces and obstacles. Named-view jumps and inspection cameras are presentation actions, not physical locomotion.
physical_contract.timestep: Use frame-rate-independent commanded movement or a fixed locomotion step; camera easing may render independently and remains interruptible.
state: Authoritative route node or walkable-surface position, facing, commanded speed and locomotion mode
Separate camera pose, selected exhibit and inspection/return snapshot
colliders: A conservative visitor capsule or declared mobility envelope
Simplified walls, case footprints and route barriers; tiny decorative meshes do not define navigation
driving: Clamp acceleration and speed to authored comfort settings; do not infer real mobility-device performance.
Project continuous movement onto the valid route surface and stop at invalid or blocked transitions.
contact: Treat walls and cases as non-penetrable route constraints with a visible stop or reroute response.
Exhibit activation uses an interaction envelope and stable ID rather than requiring pixel-perfect contact with the display mesh.
checks: Traverse each declared reachable segment with the chosen proxy and verify that it does not clip cases or cross blocked boundaries.
Stop at each exhibit and confirm the visitor envelope and declared viewing-space overlay remain distinct from the display case footprint.
Repeat travel, inspect, return and reset at two render frame rates; authoritative route and selection state must match.
